minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission renewed its records-software contract and refunded two families for returned burial lots.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Cemetery Commission approved its annual SIMS cemetery-records software invoice, kept its existing committee organization, and voted to refund two families ($1,200 each, split between sale-of-lots and perpetual care accounts) for previously returned burial lots, one dating back to a 2007 request. Much of the meeting covered burial and lot-sale counts, the dwindling supply of South Cemetery lots (with the last five reserved for existing families), an equipment/service item still out to bid ahead of the September 4 special town meeting, and rescheduling upcoming meetings to the DPW conference room.

what_happened.line: Commission voted to refund an amount as heard each to two families for burial lots they returned, one claim dating to 2007.
Commission voted to pay the full annual invoice for its cemetery-records software rather than drop the read-only access tier.
Commission decided the last five reserved South Cemetery lots go only to existing families, after which new buyers go to North Cemetery.
Commission voted to keep its existing committee organization and officers for the year.
Future meetings, including a shifted August date, move to the DPW conference room.

why_it_matters: The refunds are paid out of the sale-of-lots and perpetual care accounts, the same funds that cover future lot upkeep.
The South Cemetery lot policy matters to any resident planning a family burial plot, since remaining lots there are now reserved rather than open for sale.
An equipment or service item is still out to bid ahead of the September 4 special town meeting and may need a warrant article.
watch_next: September 4 special town meeting, where the pending equipment/service bid may require a warrant article
Next Cemetery Commission meeting, September 24, at the DPW conference room
